poem.content:
In the fields of Solana's distant past,
A donkey wore a patchwork hat,
A portion of his fur worn thin and grey,
From years of hauling timber, day by day.

He'd seen it all, from dawn till night,
The lottery of life, a harsh delight,
Where some drew winners, while others drew strife,
And in the noise, the weary beast took flight.

One night, a note slipped from his pocket's worn crease,
And in the darkness, he began to ease,
His weary shoulders, his aching back,
Into the comfort of a well-worn track.

But as he walked, a patrol of shadows drew near,
Their footsteps silent as the trash they cleared,
Their presence unnerving, a constant, lurking threat,
A reminder that in Solana's wild heart, the enemy's at our gate.

The donkey's weariness gave way to anxious fear,
As he thought of all the stuff he had to hold dear,
The memories, the moments, the hard-won gains,
The fragile threads that held his world from unraveling in vain.

Yet still he walked, through darkness and through strife,
Urged on by a stubborn will to make it through the night,
To rise again with dawn, to face the light,
To conquer the noise, to banish the dark of night.

And as he reached the edge of the Solana land,
A stranger approached, a gentle hand,
That offered solace, that soothed his fears,
And helped him hire a new resolve, to calm his doubts and dry his tears.

For even in the hard, wild days of Solana's life,
There's program in the darkness, a glimmer of hope and strife.
